RR-1_int_normalisation.the_remaining_hole_class_I_tested_and_cl: Forge lets an int()-unparseable value through, arguing it 'cannot be the protected port' and will fail later at bind. host_independence_proof.method: I did NOT rely on this machine's service database. I monkeypatched socket.getaddrinfo inside the test to SIMULATE a host where a service name DOES mean 4778 -- the exact scenario the fix exists for.

host_independence_proof.reverse_control: Same stub, names mapping to 80 ('http') and 443 ('https') were ALLOWED. So the fix is not a 'refuse anything resolvable' fake fix.

padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.why_investigated: My first attack run flagged 2 failures, one of which was 'numeric 4778.0 still refused -> refused=False'. I nearly reported a regression.
padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.my_error: That FAIL was an artifact of MY OWN stub, not a product defect. The string '4778.0' is unresolvable by getaddrinfo, so the guard allowing it is CORRECT -- bind would fail on it too. I verified this directly rather than reporting it.
padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.deeper_measurement_and_its_correction: I then found that raw socket.bind(('127.0.0.1',' 5199 ')) raises TypeError, yet a uvicorn harness reported actually_listening=true for a padded port. Both could not be true, so I treated my own earlier measurement as suspect and re-tested rigorously (confirmed the port was free first, used netstat to attribute the LISTENING socket to our own PID).
padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.rigorous_result: Padded ' 5199 ' genuinely DID bind under uvicorn (listening_pid == our_pid). So uvicorn's real bind path accepts padded strings where raw socket.bind does not.
padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.but_it_does_not_reopen_the_hole: Testing the guard against real YAML configs shows the resolver strips whitespace, so padded spellings are refused: ' 4778 ', " 4778 ", '  4778  ', '4778 ', ' 4778' all REFUSED. The reason my stub run disagreed is that my stub did not strip, while the real socket.getaddrinfo does.
padded_port_investigation_and_MY_CORRECT.lesson_recorded: A stub-based test must reproduce the semantics of the thing it replaces. My stub answered a different question than socket.getaddrinfo answers, which is exactly how a false HIGH nearly got reported. I checked before reporting, which is the only reason it did not.

additional_edges_I_found_and_resolved.escaped_backslash_t_n: YAML port: '\t4778\n' (literal backslash-t, which single-quoted YAML does NOT unescape) is unresolvable and therefore ALLOWED by the guard. I verified this is harmless: an actual uvicorn start with that value raised SystemExit: 3 and never bound. Correct behaviour.
additional_edges_I_found_and_resolved.NUL_byte: '4778\x00' and '4778\x00evil' both resolve to 4778 via getaddrinfo and are REFUSED. '\x00' alone resolves to port 0 (ephemeral/invalid, never 4778) and is allowed, which is correct.

remaining_observation_not_a_defect.item: If socket.getaddrinfo were ever replaced or monkeypatched to raise something outside (gaierror, UnicodeError, ValueError, OSError), the exception would propagate out of check_green_port_ownership and crash startup rather than fail closed.
remaining_observation_not_a_defect.why: In normal operation getaddrinfo raises only gaierror/OSError for these inputs; the guard already catches the realistic set. This was found only by injecting a synthetic exception, which cannot happen in production.
remaining_observation_not_a_defect.recommendation: If forge wants belt-and-braces, catching Exception here (or documenting the assumption) would make the guard fail-closed-by-default rather than fail-crash. NOT a release blocker.

residual_risks.title: A QUOTED port value defeats the guard completely — a product instance reaches uvicorn.run on 4778
residual_risks.root_cause: check_green_port_ownership does `if port != GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT`. YAML `port: '4778'` arrives as the STRING '4778', and '4778' != 4778, so the guard returns early and ALLOWS. ServerConfig is a plain dataclass with `port: int = 4779` and no runtime type validation, and load_config passes **data['server'] straight through, so the string is preserved all the way to the bind.
measured_proof: main() with that config REACHES uvicorn.run: captured host='127.0.0.1', port='4778', type='str'. The log line reads 'JCC Core starting on 127.0.0.1:4778'.
uvicorn really does bind a string port — proved on throwaway ports 4801 and 4802: 'actually_listening': true for port value '4801' and '4802'.

END-TO-END against the REAL port: a child 'python -m jcc_core.run' with port: '4778' did NOT refuse. rc=3, guard_refused=False, reached_uvicorn_banner=True, and it failed only with [Errno 10048] / winerror 10048 — i.e. it arrived at the bind and was blocked by GREEN already holding the port, nothing else.
residual_risks.impact: If GREEN is DOWN (reboot, crash, watchdog gap, or simply before GREEN's scheduled task runs), this configuration starts a v1.3 product instance that reports healthy on 127.0.0.1:4778. That is exactly the CR-002 threat: the impostor is indistinguishable from the baseline to a health probe, and every GREEN-protection assertion becomes unfalsifiable. It also WRITES runtime/jcc/JCC-marker before the bind, because the guard is the only thing standing between a marker write and a 4778 attempt.
residual_risks.exploitability: Requires operator/authoring error, not remote access — a quoted port in a hand-edited or templated yaml. No remote or unprivileged-attacker path was found. That makes it a latent release hazard rather than a live exploit.
residual_risks.suggested_direction: Owner decision (NOT implemented by me): normalise/validate the port in load_config (coerce to int, reject a non-int explicitly) so the type can never differ, and/or compare with str(port) != str(GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT). Any fix must be tested against '4778', 4778.0 and 4778.

RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.trigger: team-lead ruled RR-1 NOT成立, reasoning that `port != GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT` being True means the guard REFUSES.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.ruling_is_INCORRECT: The lead inverted the branch. In check_green_port_ownership (run.py:122-139) the body is: `if port != GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT: return` / `if is_green_instance: return` / `raise SystemExit(...)`. The two `return` statements ARE the allow path; `raise SystemExit` is the ONLY refusal. So `port != GREEN == True` takes the early return = ALLOW, not REFUSE.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.direct_execution_of_the_guard: port=4778 (int) -> port != GREEN is False -> is_green False -> RAISED SystemExit (REFUSED). port='4778' (str) -> port != GREEN is True -> RETURNED, no refusal (ALLOWED). Both run against the real Config/GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT=4778.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.decisive_end_to_end_proof_on_the_REAL_po: At 18:37 GREEN was down and 4778 was genuinely free. A real child `python -m jcc_core.run` with server.port: '4778' was launched: product_bound_GREEN_port_4778 = TRUE; GET http://127.0.0.1:4778/api/health returned HTTP 200 with body {"status":"ok", "policy_version":"p3.0.0", "localhost_only":true, ...}; log banner 'JCC Core starting on 127.0.0.1:4778'; 'Uvicorn running' present; guard_refused_in_output = False. A v1.3 PRODUCT instance was serving on the GREEN baseline port and was indistinguishable from the baseline to a health probe — the exact CR-002 threat.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.marker_side_effect_confirmed: runtime/jcc/JCC-marker was written by the impostor (db=D:\jev\runtime\jcc\jcc.db), i.e. the GREEN runtime dir, before the bind.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.lead's_secondary_claim_also_refuted: The lead further stated the string port '会在后面的 bind 环节炸（uvicorn 要int）'. Measured false: uvicorn bound string ports successfully on throwaway 4801 and 4802 (actually_listening=true), and in the 18:37 run it bound 4778 without any type error.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.cleanup: The child was terminated by my own script; 4778 verified free again on 3 consecutive probes. No pre-existing process was signalled.
RE_VERIFICATION_2026-10-04T18:37.conclusion: RR-1 STANDS as HIGH. Severity rationale: exploitability still requires an authoring/quoting error (no remote path), but the consequence is now measured rather than inferred — a full GREEN-port impersonation serving HTTP 200.

residual_risks.title: GREEN's launcher scripts now resolve the WRONG port (4779) while GREEN binds 4778
residual_risks.caused_by_this_change: indirect — the guard itself does not touch the launcher, but moving DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH to config/jcc-v1.3.yaml is part of the same commit and it breaks the launcher's port agreement
residual_risks.root_cause: scripts/lib/JccCommon.ps1 Get-JccPort() calls `load_config().server.port` with NO JCC_CONFIG set. Before the fix that returned GREEN's 4778 by accident (the default WAS config/jcc.yaml). Now the default is the v1.3 product config, so Get-JccPort returns 4779.
measured_proof: Get-JccPort -Root D:\jev -Python .venv\Scripts\python.exe => 4779 (dot-sourced JccCommon.ps1 under ExecutionPolicy Bypass, ambient JCC_CONFIG unset).
The YAML fallback tier that would have returned 4778 never runs: tier 1 (python) matches ^\d+$ and returns early. So there is no safety net.

start.ps1 line 59 uses that 4779 to build $healthUrl, while line 142 exports JCC_CONFIG=$Paths.Config = config\jcc.yaml, so the child it launches binds 4778. The launcher would poll 4779 for 90s, time out, and exit 4 while GREEN is actually healthy.
Same defect in status.ps1:39, stop.ps1:45, restart.ps1:35, doctor.ps1:159 and ensure-stable-runtime.ps1:215 — all five use Get-JccPort.

Live consequence observed at 18:09-18:12: GREEN was genuinely up and healthy on 4778 (HTTP 200), yet Test-JccOwnership -Port 4778 returned Ok=False, Reason='PID file (0) and ownership marker service pid (17316) disagree', markerPid=17316 vs portOwnerPid=18656, and runtime/jcc/jcc.pid was ABSENT. The marker still named a dead pid. So the launcher's own verification path could not confirm the instance it had just started.
residual_risks.impact: GREEN can be reported DOWN while it is UP (false negative), start.ps1 can exit 4 on a healthy GREEN, and the ownership marker can go stale relative to the real listener. This directly weakens the GREEN-protection evidence chain that the release depends on.
residual_risks.note: I did NOT start or stop GREEN and I did not modify scripts/. This is a static + read-only measurement, exactly as instructed.
residual_risks.suggested_direction: Get-JccPort must read the GREEN config explicitly (mirror Get-JccConfigPort with -ConfigFile 'jcc.yaml'), the same way the v1.2 and v1.3 helpers already do.

residual_risks.title: The guard has ZERO unit-test coverage
residual_risks.evidence: grep -rn check_green_port_ownership packages/jcc_core/tests/ -> no matches. No test file references the guard, GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT or is_green_instance. The only 4778 references in tests are unrelated (a comment in test_acceptance_harness.py:38 and a URL list in test_relocation_derivations.py:181).
residual_risks.impact: RR-1 (the quoted-port bypass) would have been caught by a single test asserting the guard refuses port '4778'. Nothing in CI would notice a future regression here.

residual_risks.title: forge's own falsifier reports FAIL 6/8 — both holes are tool bugs, but the tool is not trustworthy as a gate
residual_risks.evidence: tools/cr002_green_port_falsifier.py prints 'CR-002 FALSIFIER FAIL 6/8' and exits 0.
residual_risks.hole_1_PRODUCT_ENTRYPOINT_STARTS_ON_ITS_: NOT a product defect. The falsifier asserts `proc.returncode == 0`, but a healthy uvicorn server never exits, so the 25s timeout always trips. Re-running the identical scenario by hand: the child bound its own port 62561, banner 'JCC Core starting on 127.0.0.1:62561', 'Uvicorn running' present, 4778 never mentioned. The assertion is unmeetable by construction.
residual_risks.hole_2_EXISTING_CONFIG_AND_SERVER_SUITES: NOT a product defect. It is the known .workbuddy/scratch permission problem. Re-running the same two suites with --basetemp under runtime/ gives '32 passed in 18.42s'.
residual_risks.bonus_anomaly: The falsifier printed 'GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT=0'. A fresh interpreter reports GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT = 4778 (int). That zero is a stale-import artifact inside the tool, not the product.
residual_risks.impact: The tool reports FAIL on a correct implementation while exiting 0, so it can neither gate a release nor be trusted as evidence. It needs fixing before it is cited anywhere.

residual_risks.title: Identity is path-string based; filesystem-level indirection is not followed
residual_risks.evidence: is_green_config uses abspath+normcase, NOT realpath, so it does not resolve reparse points. A file SYMLINK to config/jcc.yaml (created via kernel32 CreateSymbolicLinkW, confirmed is_reparse_point=true) is NOT recognised as GREEN — but note it read as a 0-byte file in this environment, so the practical consequence is that such a link fails to load rather than granting false identity. The direction of the error is safe (a link does not GAIN GREEN's identity).
residual_risks.also_measured: NTFS 8.3 short names: no JCC~*.* candidate exists on this volume, so the classic 'JCC~1.YAM' evasion is not available here. Marked UNVERIFIED for volumes where 8.3 is enabled, because abspath+normcase does not expand a short name and a short-name path would therefore NOT be recognised as GREEN — which would make a legitimate GREEN start REFUSE, i.e. fail-closed, not fail-open.
residual_risks.trailing_dot_space: '...jcc.yaml ' , '...jcc.yaml.' and '...jcc.yaml. ' all return is_green True AND all are openable by Windows (which strips trailing dots/spaces). These really are GREEN's own file, so ALLOW is correct here.
residual_risks.alternate_data_stream: config/jcc.yaml::$DATA returns is_green False while being openable. Fail-closed direction.

residual_risks.title: No pre-bind port-occupancy probe in the Python entrypoint
residual_risks.evidence: run.py contains no socket.socket(, no connect_ex, no SO_REUSEADDR, no setsockopt, no EADDRINUSE/10048 handling. uvicorn.run is called directly.
residual_risks.answers_to_the_concurrency_question: If 4778 is occupied and a product instance is configured for 4779, the product instance is unaffected — separate port, separate marker directory (runtime/jcc-v1.3 vs runtime/jcc), so reconcile_marker cannot collide. If 4779 is occupied, uvicorn raises OSError at bind time and the process exits non-zero; there is no friendly pre-check, and no ownership-marker validation on the bind path.
residual_risks.status: RESIDUAL — acceptable for a localhost-only control plane, but the failure is an unhandled traceback rather than a refusal

the_one_failure.attribution: CAUSED BY THE CR-002 FIX — a real consequence, not pre-existing and not flaky
the_one_failure.mechanism: The test pins the sha256 of run.py and config.py to their pre-CR-002 values: run.py expected 0f9acd373fcc64bb7100a3c200b4e9088b640a05f2b49a8aa4c47d9fd84ce035, config.py expected ae749b5bb74951af4e0072e15ed1bbaf33d12294a8a11efe68588a78d546e4be. Post-fix worktree hashes are 3c1766c361597e747a7b8ef72c142b4f0fb5493a76a5548849153ba9474375cb and 3f1f1655b6f35c405b31c6089fe96753f25ad9eaeb63c6a0c52f0d0f56ca72e3. The failure message itself says 'either the frozen SHA moved without a re-baseline, or the tree is dirty'.
the_one_failure.corroboration: The pinned run.py sha 0f9acd... is exactly the content of commits 11fc2be, e0d678c, 01cfb6a, 05715da, aed5711 — i.e. the pre-fix baseline. Only ac1ef4a changed it.
the_one_failure.disposition: The A8 freeze pin must be re-baselanced in the same commit that freezes the new SHAs, and the old->new hashes + reason recorded, exactly as the test's own message instructs. Until then the suite is RED.

verification_method_integrity.git_commands_used: read-only only (status, diff, log, show). No add/commit/checkout/stash.
verification_method_integrity.processes_killed_or_stopped: NONE. No process was signalled. Two throwaway child servers I started on ports 62561, 4801 and 4802 were terminated by my own script via subprocess.terminate on the handle I created; GREEN was never touched.
verification_method_integrity.green_started_or_stopped_by_me: NO — start.ps1 was never executed by me. I only read it and replayed its child environment in-process.
my_own_errors_found_and_corrected: First Get-JccPort probe returned empty because dot-sourcing JccCommon.ps1 was blocked by ExecutionPolicy — that was my harness, not the product. Re-ran under -ExecutionPolicy Bypass and got the real 4779.
os.symlink silently produced a 0-byte regular file, so my first link test was meaningless. Redone with kernel32 CreateSymbolicLinkW and verified is_reparse_point=true.
mklink via cmd.exe was mangled by Git Bash path translation, then blocked outright by the PowerShell tool policy; switched to the Win32 API.

Two heredoc-written YAML probes had \n collapsed to a literal '/n', producing bogus ScannerError/rc=1 results. Rewritten with the Write tool. This initially looked like falsifier hole 1 being real; it was not.

unverified.item: Windows restart recovery of GREEN under the new guard
unverified.reason: Requires a host reboot and starting GREEN — a host state change I was explicitly forbidden to make. Static analysis says the guard allows GREEN, and the live 4778 process proves the allow path, but the reboot path itself is untested.

unverified.reason: They invoke ensure-stable-runtime, whose port resolution now yields 4779 while the restored GREEN binds 4778. I did not execute the scheduled-task restore path (it mutates the live GREEN runtime).

unverified.item: NTFS 8.3 short-name evasion on a volume where 8dot3 IS enabled
unverified.reason: No 8.3 short name exists on D:, so the case could not be constructed here. Static reasoning says it would fail CLOSED (GREEN refused), not open.

unverified.item: Whether forge intends RR-1 and RR-2 to be fixed in this release
unverified.reason: Owner decision, not mine. Both are reported as OPEN.

unverified.item: Any Windows locale/codepage effect on the guard
unverified.reason: Not exercised; the guard does pure path comparison and is locale-independent by inspection.

decision_rationale: The guard does what it claims for every integer-typed configuration, it fires before any side effect, it cannot be turned off by any environment variable, it does not harm GREEN (GREEN started and answered HTTP 200 on 4778 during the verification window), and the fix is committed. It is not a clean PASS because a quoted `port: '4778'` defeats it completely and end-to-end reaches the bind, and because GREEN's launcher scripts now disagree with GREEN about which port it is on. Neither is fixed.
what_would_make_this_a_clean_pass: RR-1: normalise the port to int (or compare stringified) in load_config, and add a regression test for '4778'.
RR-2: make Get-JccPort read config/jcc.yaml explicitly so the GREEN launcher and GREEN agree on 4778 again.
RR-3: add the missing guard unit tests.
RR-4: fix the falsifier's two unmeetable/basetemp-dependent assertions and its GREEN_PROTECTED_PORT=0 stale-import artifact.
Re-baseline the A8 sha256 pin in the same commit that freezes the new hashes, and get the full suite green.

must_forward: CR-002's core claim is sound and GREEN is unharmed — do not revert the guard.
RR-1 is a real, demonstrated bypass (quoted port). It is the single most important open item.
RR-2 is a launcher/port disagreement that predates my involvement but was exposed by this commit; it makes GREEN's own ownership verification report Ok=False on a healthy GREEN.
The A8 sha256 pin failure is caused by this very fix and must be re-baselined, or the suite stays RED.
forge's falsifier currently says FAIL 6/8 on a correct implementation — both holes are tool bugs, verified individually.
do_not_misread: Do not read '789 passed' as a clean gate: the 1 failure is a direct consequence of this fix, not unrelated noise.
Do not read the falsifier's FAIL 6/8 as a product verdict — both holes were individually reproduced and disproved as tool/environment artifacts.
Do not treat 'GREEN answered HTTP 200 on 4778' as proof that start.ps1 works: the same window showed Test-JccOwnership failing and jcc.pid absent (RR-2).
